preRules.note: क़ is क + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ख़ is ख + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ग़ is ग + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ज़ is ज + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ड़ is ड + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ढ़ is ढ + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
फ़ is फ + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
य़ is य + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ऩ is न + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ऱ is र + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
ऴ is ळ + nukta: the nukta is drawn as a sign of its own.
Nukta: written before its letter.

A visible virama is the halant B2 (U+FDD4 marks it for the pairs): ्+ZWNJ, and a virama that ends a word - before a space, punctuation, a danda, a digit, anything but a letter or sign of the script or a joiner, or at the end of the text. Every Unicode font draws a word-final virama as a visible halant; the half form the composer answers for a bare virama is only what it shows while it waits for the next letter.

Reph: र् before a letter is written after the letter and its signs (before a visarga; and before a sign the fonts have no glyph for, which the table passes through - Word draws it on a dotted circle of its own, and the reph belongs on its letter); U+FDD0 marks it for the pairs. र्+ZWJ is the eyelash ra, ऱ् the half ra.
श्र्य त्र्य with a vowel sign: the half श्र् त्र् and य, as with a ZWJ.
Ya-sign after a conjunct of three letters or more, with no sign: E7 (U+FDD8 marks it).
Ya-sign after a conjunct of two letters, with no sign or a vowel sign: E7 (U+FDD6 marks it; त्त्य is written with the half त्त there).
Ya-sign with a vowel sign (not the i-sign): E7 (U+FDD7 marks it).
Ya-sign: after ट ठ ड ढ ्य is always the ya-sign E7.
Ya-sign: ्य alone is the ya-sign E7 (U+FDD2 marks it) - but before ि ं ँ ः, a reph or the ra-sign the composer writes the half letter and य.
Ra-sign: ्र after a letter (U+FDD3 marks it for the pairs).
The i-sign is written before its letter or conjunct (Unicode logical order -> visual order).
A virama before a vowel letter or a sign (a word-final one is the halant, above): the composer writes the half form it is waiting with (U+FDD5 marks it for the pairs).

A conjunct with a virama after it (waiting for its next letter, or with one more) is written as half letters, not as a ligature - the composer breaks क्क into क् क् when a link follows: as if each virama but the last had a ZWJ.

postRules.note: U+FDDD stands for a joiner: no glyph, and nothing for the rules below to stop at.
Va after ङ छ ट ठ ड ढ: the va-sign 89 under the letter.
Signs below and above a letter, and the reph, go before its spacer 24.
Signs below a letter go before its spacer 3E.
ञ त्त after a letter with the halant: a sign below takes the 3E spacer in place of the 6D stem.
Ra-sign after the va-sign or a ligature of ट ठ ड ढ: after the spacer.
u after द ह and their ligatures: FE.
uu after द ह and their ligatures: FF.
u under a stacked ligature or a nukta: the short 78.
Ra-sign under the round-bottomed letters and ळ: B4.
Ra-sign B4 + vocalic r: the sign after the spacer.
i-sign over one letter or ligature: 7B (5B only over र and alone).
i-sign over a conjunct of two glyphs: the long 70.
Candrabindu after a tall sign (i, ii, e, ai): moved right by two 3E.
U+FDD1 in a pair keeps the rules above off a spelling the composer writes its own way; it is not text.
